question: A 37-year-old African-American man presents to his primary care provider with a history of fatigue and nausea that started about 6 months ago. His symptoms have slowly gotten worse and now he has trouble climbing the stairs to his 3rd floor apartment without resting. Past medical history is significant for poorly controlled HIV and a remote history of heroin addiction. Today his temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), the blood pressure is 118/72 mm Hg, and the pulse is 75/min. Physical examination reveals morbid obesity and 1+ pitting edema of both lower extremities. Urine dipstick reveals 2+ proteinuria. Urinalysis shows no abnormal findings. Which of the following is the most likely etiology of this patient condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: HIV infection -> increased risk of kidney disease -> proteinuria -> 70% CHAIN: Morbid obesity -> increased risk of kidney disease -> proteinuria -> 60% CHAIN: Pitting edema -> fluid overload -> proteinuria -> 50% CHAIN: 2+ proteinuria on urine dipstick -> glomerular damage -> kidney disease -> 80% CHAIN: 1+ pitting edema of both lower extremities -> fluid retention -> kidney disease -> 70% CHAIN: African-American ethnicity -> higher risk for focal segmental glomerulosclerosis -> likely etiology -> Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis -> 70%
analysis: Given the patient's presentation of fatigue, nausea, difficulty climbing stairs, morbid obesity, pitting edema, and proteinuria, along with a history of poorly controlled HIV and heroin addiction, the most likely etiology of his condition is focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS). FSGS is commonly associated with HIV infection and obesity, leading to proteinuria and edema.
